h1: Electrical Safety Inspections in South Florida
intro: If your carrier wants a 4-point inspection, or something just feels off, an inspection is the honest answer. Our licensed crew walks your panel, meter socket, and wiring the way a Florida carrier does, then tells you what is sound and what is likely to get flagged.

definition.heading: What is an electrical safety inspection
definition.body: A defined inspection of your electrical system, not a sales visit. A licensed electrician checks the panel and breakers, the meter socket, the grounding, and the visible wiring, the same things a Florida carrier cares about in a 4-point.

symptoms.title: A carrier asking for a 4-point inspection
symptoms.body: Electrical is where older homes get flagged. A documented inspection gives the carrier the record it wants, and tells you where you stand first.

symptoms.title: An older home you have never had checked
symptoms.body: Codes have changed several times since the house was wired. An inspection tells you whether it kept up or quietly fell behind.

symptoms.title: Warm outlets, flickering lights, or a buzzing panel
symptoms.body: These are the system telling you something. An inspection finds the source before it turns into heat or fire.

symptoms.title: A panel you have heard is a problem brand
symptoms.body: Some brands have a known history of trouble, and it is often exactly what a carrier flags. An inspection confirms what you have.

process.title: The call and a few honest questions
process.body: You tell us the home's age, what you have noticed, and why you want the inspection.

process.title: The walkthrough and assessment
process.body: The panel, breakers, meter socket, grounding, and visible wiring, checked in person.

process.title: One clear, honest report of what we found
process.body: What is fine, what to watch, what needs attention, and what a carrier is likely to flag.

process.title: Repairs, permits, and inspection where needed
process.body: Our own crew can handle any repair, priced separately, permit and inspection included.

benefits.title: A clear answer, in plain language
benefits.body: Exactly where your system stands, explained the way you would explain it to family.

benefits.title: Small problems caught early
benefits.body: A warm connection found today is a quick fix, not the much bigger bill it becomes later.

benefits.title: Ready for a carrier's questions
benefits.body: You learn what a 4-point would flag on your own timeline, not from a non-renewal notice.

benefits.title: Peace of mind you can act on
benefits.body: Sound or not, you know the truth about the power running through your home.

localSections.heading: The transitions of South Florida housing
localSections.body: Florida homes span many eras, each wired to the standards of its time. A 1960s house may still have its original panel and grounding, and the 80s and 90s brought their own problem brands. We read your system against its era.

localSections.heading: What Florida insurance carriers are asking for
localSections.body: Many Florida carriers require a 4-point before they write or renew on an older home, and an aging panel, problem brand, or outdated wiring is what gets flagged. A documented inspection is the record they want, on your timeline rather than an underwriter's.

guide.title: The honest guide to an electrical safety inspection in South Florida

sections.heading: What an inspection is, and the 4-point behind it
sections.body: A defined inspection, not a consultation or a sales call. We examine the panel and breakers, the meter socket, the grounding, and the visible wiring. If a carrier asked for a 4-point, electrical is where older homes get flagged, and it is the part we know cold.

sections.heading: The honest cadence, and what we look at
sections.body: Here is what most companies will not tell you: most homes do not need this often. Once every five years suits the average home, since codes update on a multi-year cycle. Older homes and homes with pools are the exception. We separate what is merely old from what is truly unsafe.

sections.heading: What happens if we find something
sections.body: If we find a problem, you get exactly what it is and how serious, then you choose your timing with no pressure. Want it fixed? Our in-house crew handles it, priced separately, permit included. If we find nothing, we say so just as plainly.

faqs.question: My insurance company wants a 4-point inspection. Can you help?
faqs.answer: Yes. A documented inspection from a licensed master electrician is often exactly the record a carrier wants for the electrical portion of a 4-point. We inspect the panel, meter, grounding, and wiring, then tell you what is likely to get flagged.

faqs.question: How often should I have an electrical safety inspection?
faqs.answer: About once every five years for a typical home, since codes update on a multi-year cycle. Older homes and homes with pools warrant closer attention. We will tell you honestly if you do not need us again for years.

faqs.question: What does an inspection include?
faqs.answer: The panel and breakers, the meter socket, the grounding, and the visible wiring and connections. You get a plain answer on what is fine, what to watch, and what needs attention.

faqs.question: Will you just try to sell me a bunch of work?
faqs.answer: No. If your system is sound, we say so and you are done. We do not invent work.

pricing.display: Quoted as a defined scope when you book
